messages:
alejandro: Hey folks, first-day onboarding question. I followed the kubernetes setup doc but `kubectl` is failing with a cert error when I try to list pods in our sandbox namespace:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n sandbox-ale
Error from server: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```
I grabbed the kubeconfig from the onboarding page and put it in ~/.kube/config. Not sure what to try next. :confused:

morgan: welcome! Two quick things to check: 1) if you have a corporate proxy or VPN split-tunnel it can interfere with cluster CA; 2) `KUBECONFIG` env var might be pointing at a merged file that has an old cert. Run `echo $KUBECONFIG` and `kubectl config view --minify --raw` to see the cert-data in the current context.

alejandro: KUBECONFIG is empty. I only have ~/.kube/config. `kubectl config view --raw` shows two clusters both named `redwood-dev` (weird) and the cert-authority-data looks different between them.

morgan: ah that happens when someone manually concatenates configs. You can flatten to a single clean one: 
```
kubectl config view --flatten --minify > /tmp/clean-kubeconfig && KUBECONFIG=/tmp/clean-kubeconfig kubectl get nodes
```
If that still gives the same cert error, it's likely your laptop is routing through the corporate proxy which rewrites certs. Try `curl -v https://10.12.34.56:6443` and see if the TLS cert subject matches the cluster CN. If you can't hit the control plane IP directly, you may need to SSH tunnel via the bastion host. Ping infra if so.

alejandro: tried flattening, same error. `curl` shows a proxy banner. I'm on corp-network.

morgan: ok that explains it. Two options: 1) add the cluster CA to your OS trust store (not ideal), or 2) use our bastion SOCKS proxy for kubectl: 
```
ssh -D 1080 bastion@jump.redwood.local -N
export ALL_PROXY=socks5://localhost:1080
KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config kubectl get pods -n sandbox-ale
```
We usually recommend the bastion approach for laptop dev.

infra-bot: Access request #AK-13042 created (user alejandro) for namespace sandbox-ale. Approver: @jess. Status: pending. Link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/AK-13042

jess: Hi @alejandro, I can approve once your manager confirms. For RBAC we add you to `sandbox-developers` which gives `edit`. Do you need `edit` or just `view`? Also, if you use the bastion approach, let us know and we can add a note to your ticket so infra ops doesn't block the proxy route.

alejandro: edit would be helpful for iterating on local manifests. I'll ping my manager for approval now. Also planning to use the bastion.

jess: Approved and bound. You should have access now. Note: we added a ticket comment to allow bastion SOCKS for your IP for 30d.

alejandro: confirmed I can list pods and port-forward now. `kubectl auth can-i create deployments -n sandbox-ale` returns `yes`. Thanks for the quick help — saved me a ton of time :tada:
